chapter: Leo Watson and the Panassie sessions
title: Mezz Mezzrow as leader and his habits
summary: Mezzrow called the session; Bunn got along with him but disliked his pot habit, which made Mezz sloppy and unreliable.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Do you remember Panassié calling this particular session? I think Mezzrow was the leader.
Milton Mezzrow.
Milton Mezzrow was the leader on the date.
Yeah. He was the one that called the session.
I see. Do you remember that at all,
like when that -- that was in '38. I don't know --
It was in '38.
Yeah. You would have been working with the Spirits, I guess.
Yes.
And -- can you remember that at all, the actual session?
Well, whatever you want to say about it, if I can remember it I'll sure tell you.
Well, some people -- for example, it's been claimed that you and Mezzrow didn't get along too well. Is that true?
Well, no.
Uh-huh.
No. Mezzrow and I was all right.
Uh-huh.
As far as that's concerned. As far as his habits was concerned, I wasn't interested.
What do you mean?
Well, he had a habit, you know.
Oh, you mean drugs.
Pot.
Oh, I see. You think it affected his playing, or --
No.
Just his attitude.
Oh, maybe it did, too, because he did sometimes when he wanted to play play some tunes that he knew, evidently.
Uh-huh.
That was it. And then a lot of things he would miss all the time.
Uh-huh.
And that's what used to bring us all down in the band, far as that's concerned, because Mezz didn't have his instrument punctual.
Uh-huh. He was sloppy.
Yeah.
